items.key: ai:what is the no-spend challenge? the viral money saving trend that could help you reset your financial habits
items.text: What is the no-spend challenge? The viral money saving trend that could help you reset your financial habits
items.article: The challenge, which first emerged on TikTok, is starting a conversation about saving cash Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Amid relentless commercial advertising urging continuous purchasing, the viral "no-spend challenge" provides a practical way to resist mindless consumerism. Rather than simply converting the traditional virtue of thriftiness into a social media trend, the movement enables individuals to recognise the impulse triggers that prompt unnecessary purchases, helping them break negative spending cycles. Louise Hill, founder of the pocket money and financial education app GoHenry, describes the trend as an effective way to reset personal finances . She explains, "The no-spend challenge is a financial reset which is when you commit to spending zero money on non-essential items for a set period. "It shows you where you spend your money, so that you take more accountability for your purchases. It creates a really clear categorisation in your mind about what your true ‘needs’ are versus your ‘wants’." Hill also views the practice as a constructive method for developing essential money management skills. She adds, "By learning to prioritise your spending and delaying instant gratification, it’s a really useful way of testing yourself and taking back control. Turning it into a challenge is a fun and interesting way to do it – it’s a more positive way of saving money."

The Norwegian Nobel Committee will announce the winner in Oslo on October 9. It received 287 candidates this year – 208 individuals and 79 organisations. items.article: Tottenham youngster is pushing for further first-team involvement Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice . Tottenham youngster Luca Williams-Barnett took another step forward in his development earlier this week when he was included in the club’s first-team squad photo. Having travelled on the club’s pre-season tour Down Under over the summer , Williams-Barnett is now officially part of Roberto De Zerbi ’s first-team squad. Described by the Spurs boss as “a potential top player”, the electric young winger is pushing for further first-team involvement after making his senior debut under Thomas Frank last season. De Zerbi has been reluctant to use Spurs’ academy players so far and, surprisingly, left Williams-Barnett at home as his side crashed out of the Carabao Cup away to Liverpool last month .
